Summary: Perseverance of the Saints teaches that those truly united to Christ will be kept by God's power and will endure in faith to the end. It gives assurance not from human strength, but from God's faithfulness to complete His saving work.
HistoricalDevelopment: Rooted in Augustine's teaching on the gift of perseverance and affirmed by the Reformers, it was stated as the fifth point in the Canons of Dort (1618-1619).
Interpretations: Reformed Christians teach true believers cannot finally fall away, while Arminian, Wesleyan, and many other Christians warn that believers should heed Scripture's warnings and may teach the possibility of apostasy.
RelatedPeople: Augustine; Calvin; Dort Synod; John Owen
